name: Religion in American Life

summary.text: Religion in American Life Inc. was a New York nonprofit of business and professional people, active from 1949, that sponsored the Ad Council's annual 'Religion in American Life' advertising campaign urging church attendance; its president described its aim as interreligious rather than ecumenical. A 1952 trade-press item said the campaign made clergymen more favourably disposed to business and advertising.

sources.title: Doctoral dissertation on the Religion in American Life campaign (Henning, 1996)

facts.claim: RIAL is described in a 1986 Christian Science Monitor report as a nonprofit group of business and professional people based in New York, active since 1949, whose president said its aim was interreligious with no denominational ties.
facts.quote: a nonprofit group of business and professional people based here in New York that has been active since 1949

facts.claim: A 1952 issue of Sponsor magazine inferred from a survey of clergymen that the 'Religion in American Life' campaign moved them to be more favorably disposed to business and advertising.
facts.quote: moved these important molders of public opinion to be more favorably disposed to business and advertising

facts.claim: A 1996 University of Tennessee dissertation says the group was primarily concerned with helping houses of worship with membership and fund-raising drives, and that funding problems led the Ad Council to distance itself in 1992.
facts.quote: primarily concerned with helping houses of worship in their membership and fund-raising drives

sources.title: Doctoral dissertation on the Religion in American Life campaign (Henning, 1996)

connections.claim: The Ad Council carried RIAL's campaign from 1949.
connections.quote: under the low-profile sponsorship of Religion in American Life Inc.

openQuestions: Who the corporate members and donors of RIAL Inc. were is not in opened sources; the Henning (1996) dissertation and the Duke Ad Council archive would have them.
